A ratiometric linear Hall sensor reports a magnetic field relative to its
own supply voltage, and a small magnet's field falls off steeply — and
nonlinearly — with distance. This experiment characterizes that nonlinear
curve, uses it to pick a working range by an explicit criterion rather than
a guess, shows exactly what the ratiometric property buys against a
drifting supply, and then puts the sensor on [the cantilever
beam](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd) to measure tip displacement — a second,
independent route to the beam's stiffness that
[M1's](../M1-strain-load/index.qmd) strain measurement also reaches, so the
two can be checked against each other.

The beam's own dimensions are not decided (see [the beam
rig](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd#sec-beam-design)); every relation here is
symbolic in the same way, and the numbers the analysis templates print come
from placeholder values in `tools/synth/params/m2.yaml` — the same
placeholders `tools/synth/params/m1.yaml` uses for the shared rig — clearly
marked and disclosed by the synthetic-data banner on every page that uses
them.

## What you measure {#sec-m2-index-measure}

| Quantity | How | Where it is used later |
|---|---|---|
| Nonlinear calibration curve $V(d)$ | A magnet swept on a micrometer stage | Every displacement this experiment recovers |
| Resolution and curvature against $d$ | Derived from the fitted curve and S1's noise floor | The working-range choice |
| Ratiometric vs. absolute supply sensitivity | The same displacement held fixed, supply deliberately drifted | Quantifies what dividing by $V_\mathrm{cc}$ buys |
| Tip displacement under known loads | The sensor on the beam, the same masses [M1](../M1-strain-load/index.qmd) uses | The stiffness cross-check with M1 |

: What M2 produces {#tbl-m2-index-outputs}

## Bench {#sec-m2-index-bench}

**Tier 3.** [The cantilever beam rig](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd), a
micrometer stage, a ratiometric linear Hall sensor and a small magnet, and a
way to log the sensor's supply voltage on a second channel.

**Board.** Any supported board works; nothing here needs streaming timing
quality beyond what [S1](../S1-daq-static/index.qmd) already characterizes.

**Host.** Any — this experiment does not depend on host-timing effects the
way S1/S2/S3 do.

## Reference data {#sec-m2-index-data}

Seventeen generated runs ship with the experiment, in `data/`:

| File(s) | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cal-d0002` … `cal-d0020` (12 runs) | The magnet swept from 2 mm to 20 mm, sensor output and supply voltage together |
| `supply-drift` | Displacement held fixed, supply voltage deliberately drifted |
| `crosscheck-000` … `crosscheck-030` (4 runs) | The same small reference masses [M1](../M1-strain-load/index.qmd) uses, applied at the beam tip |

: Reference data shipped with M2 {#tbl-m2-index-data}

::: {.callout-warning}
## The reference data is synthetic

It is produced by a seeded generator (`tools/synth/m2_hall_displacement.py`)
whose parameters — including every beam dimension — are plausible
placeholders, not measurements, marked `TODO (Paolo)` in
`tools/synth/params/m2.yaml`. It exists so the analysis templates render,
and are checked in continuous integration, with no bench attached. Every
page that uses it says so.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
## Instructor summary {.instructor-note}

Three hours, tier 3, needs S1 as a prerequisite and is most rewarding paired
with M1, whose reference data this experiment's stiffness cross-check reads
back directly. Full notes, expected values, common failures and the rubric
are in the [handbook](handbook.qmd#sec-m2-instructor).
:::
